audit_findings.title: Acquisition-driven growth may be modeled without its required reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $309.5 million of 2025 acquisition cash, equal to 51.1% of the $606.2 million OE anchor; required recurring adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired growth enters the forecast growth rate, while acquisition payments are excluded from operating owner earnings and therefore from reinvestment deductions.
audit_findings.evidence: Over the last three years, we have completed 94 acquisitions, including 26 acquisitions in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition spending and 4.1% acquired revenue contribution are demonstrated. It remains unresolved how much of the 8%-10% forecast requires acquisitions and what recurring purchase cost supports it. Because the observed acquisition spending is large relative to owner earnings, extrapolating acquired growth without its investment could materially overstate distributable cash and intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Decompose each scenario into organic and acquired growth, support the organic component independently, and rerun the DCF after deducting the recurring acquisition investment required for any acquired-growth component.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is a senior claim missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $44.921 million at June 30, 2026, or $0.09 per diluted share; 0.40% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid holdbacks and earnouts are acquisition-related claims on cash that should reduce the equity bridge when their settlement is not included in forecast owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company had $ 37.1 million and $ 21.0 million of acquisition holdback and earnout liabilities payable to former owners of acquired companies, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates a $44.921 million liability, and the supplied bridge does not show a corresponding deduction. The omission overstates common-equity value, but the maximum direct correction is only about $0.09 per share versus the $23.37 base value and cannot alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 liability to any amounts already captured in owner earnings, then deduct the uncovered $44.921 million from the bridge and refresh per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Anchor interest expense may not represent the latest debt-funded claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.442 million pre-tax difference between the filed $40 million 2026 outlook and $28.558 million FY2025 expense; approximately $8.593 million after tax and at most about $0.37 per share across the supplied cases
audit_findings.mechanism: Because debt principal is not deducted, the higher current interest burden must reduce equity-level owner earnings in the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, interest expense, net increased $0.9 million compared to the prior year, due to the increase in the average debt balance associated primarily with the issuance of our 2035 Senior Notes, as well as borrowings under our commercial paper program.
audit_findings.explanation: The record demonstrates that current interest expense is running above the FY2025 amount: first-half 2026 expense was $18.242 million, trailing-twelve-month expense was $33.624 million, and management expects approximately $40 million for 2026. Using the filed outlook and 24.9% tax rate, the implied anchor correction produces no more than roughly $0.37 per share, far below the $9.83 gap between market price and bull value.
audit_findings.action: Normalize the anchor using the final FY2026 net interest expense, apply the associated tax effect, and rerun all scenarios while continuing to treat debt principal consistently with the equity-level OE method.

audit_findings.title: The dilution ceiling may double-count existing or already-used shares
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum disputed increment of 3.310 million shares, 0.68% of the 484.455404 million denominator; at most approximately $0.18 per share in the bull case
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential double-counting inflates fully diluted shares and mechanically depresses intrinsic value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Initially, a maximum of 1,000,000 shares of the Company’s common stock are authorized for issuance under the ESPP.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether every unvested award and the full initial ESPP authorization remains incremental is unresolved. Even the conservative upper bound—removing all 2.310 million awards and 1.000 million ESPP shares—changes the denominator by less than 0.7% and raises the bull value by only about $0.18 per share, which cannot alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile issued restricted shares, unissued RSUs and PSUs, performance assumptions, and remaining ESPP capacity to the July 13, 2026 cover-page share count, then refresh the denominator.

audit_findings.title: A non-operating gain may remain in normalized owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.332 million pre-tax; approximately $1.751 million after tax and at most about $0.08 per share across the supplied cases
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the nonrecurring gain inflates the owner-earnings anchor and all forecast cash flows derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: During the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, other (income) expense, net increased $2.7 million primarily due to higher gains on sales of non-operational assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The $2.332 million gain is demonstrated, but whether the owner-earnings calculation already removed it remains unresolved. Applying the filed 24.9% tax rate and scaling the supplied DCF cases gives a maximum effect of roughly $0.08 per share, immaterial relative to both scenario values and the market-price gap.
audit_findings.action: Trace the gain through the owner-earnings worksheet; if it remains in the $606.2 million anchor, remove its after-tax effect and rerun the scenarios.
